newsitem.title: USA: No verdict yet in New York mob case.
newsitem.headline: No verdict yet in New York mob case.

text.p: A federal jury ended a second day of deliberations Thursday without reaching a verdict in the murder and racketeering trial of accused New York City mob boss Vincent "The Chin" Gigante.
The jury of four men and eight women is weighing 21 charges against Gigante, the reputed head of the Genovese crime family.

During the deliberations, the jurors requested to be read back testimony by three of the six mob informants who testified in the trial -- Salvatore "Sammy the Bull" Gravano, Phil "Crazy Phil" Leonetti and former Luchesse crime family boss Al D'Arco.
The jury also asked to hear a series of tapes secretly recorded at a Hoboken, New Jersey restaurant owned by a former Genovese crime family member.
The government claims the tapes prove the existence of a murder plot ordered by Gigante against Gambino godfather John Gotti. The plot was never carried out.

Gotti was convicted in 1992 of murder and racketeering, largely on the testimony of Gravano, a former Gambino underboss who turned government informant. Gotti is serving life in prison without parole.
Gigante is accused of ordering seven murders, plotting to kill three other people, bid-rigging and extortion.
The jury heard testimony from a half dozen informants and a dozen law enforcement agents during almost four weeks in Brooklyn federal court before Judge Jack Weinstein.

Gigante's defence attorneys argued the informants were willing to modify their testimony to suit the government. They also argued that Anthony "Fat Tony" Salerno was convicted of being the Genovese crime family boss in 1986.
They said Gigante -- who earned the nickname "The Oddfather" for wandering the neighbourhood around his Greenwich Village apartment in a tattered bathrobe -- is incapacitated by mental illness.
But prosecutors say Gigante has feigned illness for years to avoid prosecution.
Deliberations were scheduled to resume on Friday morning.
